notes.title: Anniversary Update // Devlog + Patch Notes
notes.notes:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]We want to celebrate the one year anniversary of Cartel Tycoon leaving Early Access with an [b]Anniversary Update[/b] and some goodies for all of you![/h3]

[previewyoutube=4f49PNsC35k;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Devlog script: [/h3]
[expand type=details]Hola Capos! 

My name is Andrey, and I’m the community manager of Cartel Tycoon. We have a huge date this week - July 26 will mark one year since the 1,0 Release. Since then, we have had a lot of updates: we introduced multiple new mechanics, balanced existing ones, made new Lieutenants, and, of course, listened closely to your feedback.

We want to celebrate one year anniversary of Cartel Tycoon leaving Early Access with an update and with some goodies for all of you! Let’s get right into it! If you’re watching this before July 28, you can playtest the San Rafaela map on Steam! Leave a like on this video if you want a vacation there… 

So, it’s been one year since we left Early Access. Since then, we’ve published four major updates to the game and are working on another one right now, not including the San Rafaela DLC. The update we’re publishing today is a tad smaller, but it is still very important because we’ve wanted to focus on your feedback. 

First off, optimization. It’s been quite some time since we optimized the game, so we wanted to push the optimization further with this update. In particular, we’ve focused on the late game. Some of you know that when you build A LOT of buildings, the FPS takes a major hit. Or used to take it. Now, where you used to get 18 fps, you can get 50! Our internal tests were very promising, so we hope that you’ll feel these changes and they will lead to a much more comfortable experience! 

Secondly, balance. The introduction of the Combat System, in some cases, made the game harder than we expected, especially for new players, so we wanted to address the issue with this update further. Firstly, we wanted to address Terror and the situations when defending your building from an Enemy Gang would lead to activating the Attention Star, and defending your building from the Police would activate another, and you would be stuck in the loop of everyone constantly attacking you. Now, fights in buildings generate Terror at a much slower rate. 


Another issue with Terror was Guerrillas and Allied Gangs generating it for you even if your LTs left the fight leading to cases when your allies were responsible for your downfall. In this update, Guerrillas and Allied Gangs will leave the encounter if there are no player Liutenants in the fight AND if their Power is lower than the Power of your Enemy. We’ve also made Guerrilla convoys stronger - they now have 8 power instead of 5.

 
We’ve also upped the Allegiance of Enemy Gangs at the start of the game, so they won’t start to attack you when you’re just building your first production chain.


Another thing we’ve changed with the update is the Evacuation. Now, if you decide to leave your injured Lieutenant in the fight, you’ll be able to evacuate them for free after the fight ends - a reward for taking a risk! 


We’ve also changed Area Depots. This building used to be very powerful from the get-go, so we initially nerfed it a bit but also added it to the Research Tree so that you can upgrade as your Empire and your needs grow! 

There are smaller changes and, of course, bug fixes in the update, and you can read the full list in the Patch Notes that will be published with the update! 

Another thing we’ve added with the update are shine new Anniversary Emblems for your Cartel! You can select them at the start of your run, and they are available to everyone! 


After this release, we’ll be taking a small break in August - we’ve been working non-stop since last summer and want to refill our Endurance meter with a small vacation. But we’ll be back in the second half of August to continue our work on the San Rafaela DLC!

And we don’t want to leave you only with this update, so on July 28, this Friday, we’ll announce a contest that will let you not only win a free copy of San Rafaela DLC and get it on release but also will let you be a part of the DLC. Excited? Leave a comment if you are!   

Thank you for your support during this year and through the years of Early Access, Capos. We won’t be able to be here today without your support. We hope that you’ll enjoy the anniversary update and are excited about the San Rafaela DLC (wishlist now)! 

As always, my name is Andrey. If you enjoyed this devlog, join our Discord, follow us on Socials, and leave a like on this video. Have a lovely day, Capos. Bye-bye. 
[/expand]

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]

[h2]Major Changes[/h2]

ːcartel_nothing_personalː [b]Gang Alliances. [/b]Convince Enemy Gangs to enter into an Alliance with your Cartel! They will provide firepower in combat, won’t attack you, and even let you use buildings in their region! But be cautious. You’re not the only one that can break off an Alliance…
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/6176db26fe372065bdf8d8c80ed822340d0e5e9b.gif[/img]

ːcartel_nothing_personalː [b]Enforcers vs. Enemy Gangs.[/b] Why should you be the only one that gets blamed for everything? Now when Terror rises, Enemy Gangs, their cities, and their buildings will also become a target.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/5f0d1a13944a0e16f2f71a1ceb045eb00f7cf5ca.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/837a087a4de5dcacde260bf10dafe59602369fb8.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/f1d97cd1eeae00bdb10e9ebbc1b7a1c86f38ba02.gif[/img]

[h2]Other Updates & Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Enemy Gang City loses power when their convoy is out of it. [/b]Use new combat mechanics to attack the Enemy Gang City when they least expect it! 
[*] [b]Updated Global Unlocks Menu.[/b] Added different categories for easier navigation, added cinematic category.

notes.title: June Update this week!
notes.notes:
[h3]Hola Capos! [/h3]

Our [b]June Update is coming this week[/b], and it brings new gameplay mechanics, Balance and UI changes, and bug fixes! We’ve also made some adjustments after our Steam Weekend Playtest, so stick around even if you played it! 

[h2]First off, Gang Alliances! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/6176db26fe372065bdf8d8c80ed822340d0e5e9b.gif[/img]
Alliance is a powerful tool that can be used for protection and for strategic advancement. After our Combat Update, we’ve heard you loud and clear that Enemy Gangs could become unreasonably annoying in early and mid-game, so we’ve not only made balance changes but are introducing Gang Alliances that should help with that matter. 

Gang Alliance means that your Allied Gang will stop attacking you, their buildings (including Smuggling Points!) will become available to you, and they even will help you out during Combat! There’s a list of things you need to achieve before being able to strike an Alliance, and you’ll need to keep a close eye on your new friends because, in the world of Cartel Tycoon, they can become enemies really fast. 

After the playtest, we’ve adjusted some things to make achieving an Alliance a bit harder but also made Alliend Gang convoys faster to redeploy. 

[h2]Second, Enforcers vs. Enemy Gangs![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/5f0d1a13944a0e16f2f71a1ceb045eb00f7cf5ca.gif[/img]
Now Terror affects not only your Cartel but Enemy Gangs too! Enforcers have a chance to attack your enemies instead of you on each trigger of an Attention Star! You can use that to your advantage and capture Enemy buildings while they’re busy with the officials! 

And if the enforcers win the fight - Enemy Gangs will lose power, making it easier for you to make an Alliance or destroy them! 

After the playtest, we’ve made some adjustments to this mechanic and Enemy Gang’s behavior in general! 

[h2]Third, New Gang Agreement UI! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/f1d97cd1eeae00bdb10e9ebbc1b7a1c86f38ba02.gif[/img]
Gang Agreements are no longer a dialogue - it’s an easy-to-read menu! 

After the playtest, we’ve made some small adjustments to the menu, so it will be more clear when a new level of Agreement opens to you! 

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[b]We’ve reworked how you can attack with weapons![/b] Now, if your lieutenant is in a building that has weapons inside, the game will automatically offer to take weapons if you send them to attack an enemy! It works even when you select multiple LTs! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/901766eff364aef55b5056289e5f24055b1ca060.gif[/img]

[b]We’ve also expanded the Tutorial![/b] Get ready for more missions that will explain combat and Enemy Gang relations better! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/837a087a4de5dcacde260bf10dafe59602369fb8.gif[/img]

[b]Global Unlocks Menu is now easier to navigate![/b] Your unlocks will now be in different categories, so you don’t always have to scroll the full list if you want to change a skin for your character! And now you can watch unlocked cinematics again! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/00b12f71e1fc6d91a30593bb902acd76e126df36.gif[/img]

We’ve made smaller adjustments to new mechanics and squished some nasty bugs! The update is coming soon, and we’ll provide the patch notes with all the changes, as usual! 

[h3]Thank you for participating in the playtest and providing your feedback! ːcartel_loveː

See you soon, Capos!  [/h3]

notes.title: Fight & Stash Update // Devlog 25
notes.notes:
[h2]Hola Capos![/h2] 

[h3]The first major update of 2023 is almost here, and today I’ll tell you all about what’s inside. Aand when it’s coming out. And when you can enter the playtest to try the update before the release! 

[b]Watch the devlog right now![/b]

[previewyoutube=WpBE0xA9AuU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Hola Capos! It’s me, once again. The first major update of 2023 is almost here, and today I’ll tell you all about what’s inside. Aand when it’s coming out. Aaand when you can enter the playtest to try the update before the release. Let’s get right into it. 

[h3][b]I. FIGHT ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

First, let’s talk about the long-awaited rework of combat. The core is still the same - you win if you have more power, no tricks here. But in the new system power is not everything. [b]And if you’re not careful enough - you can lose any fight.[/b] We want combat to be more impactful and require some strategic planning beforehand.

[b]Your Lieutenants are playing a crucial role in the reworked combat[/b]. They can be injured during the fight, they can lose their power, some of them can run away from the battlefield, while others will fight to their dying breath. It’s no longer just about winning the fight with more power points - it’s about building a team with different tactics in mind.

Every Lieutenant now has an Endurance bar which depletes during a fight. The lower it is - the higher the chance to acquire a certain debuff: power loss, injury, or even an arrest. After the fight ends Lieutenants must rest for a bit to refill their Endurance, certain buildings like Residencies or Hotels will speed up this process! 

Power loss and Arrest are pretty self-explanatory but you’re probably wondering how an [b][i]“Injury”[/i][/b] will work. When your Lieutenant is injured during a fight their power no longer counts, so it can be a pretty big blow to your operation! And you also have a choice - you can evacuate your injured Lieutenant from the fight immediately. It will cost some money, of course, but they will be safely recovering in one of your buildings. Or you can decide to leave them on the battlefield. If you win the fight, you’ll still have time to evacuate them. But if you lose… they will die. 

Because Lieutenants are so crucial in the reworked combat system, [b]we made more than 10 new abilities for them and reworked some old ones[/b]. The Coordinator ability is much more useful now! Some of the new abilities are active, some are passive. For example, some of your Lieutenants fight better when they’re alone, and some will make everyone else more powerful. Certain Lieutenants will also acquire buffs to their power instead of debuffs if their Endurance is low. 

We want combat to be much more meaningful and refined, and we want to test it out with all of you before the public release, but that’s not the only thing coming with this update. 

 With a more complex combat system, we’re also introducing a new illegal resource - Weapons. You can’t grow weapons on your farms but you’ll be able to buy them from certain places like Guerillas and Enemy Gangs. Weapons give a boost to your overall power in combat and allow you to perform powerful attacks that can change the tide of the fight. Weapons are optional combat and they are pretty expensive but they can certainly help you out in fights you had no chance of winning without them! 

There are a lot of nuances, a lot of new abilities, and smaller changes that are connected to the Combat Rework. If I listed them all here, this video would’ve been longer than the Godfather trilogy. But I know that all of you are eager to know more and that’s why we’ll be publishing a more detailed guide to the new system in the coming days. And, of course, all of the changes will be listed in the Patch Notes.

But Combat is only half of the update. So let’s get to the second part. 

[h3][b]II. STASH ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

We all know that money can be Dirty or Clean. by the mid-game you can be swimming in Dirty Cash which sounds nice, but also brings a lot of attention to you. Your Selling Points are overflowing, and you’re frantically putting all of your excess Dirty Money in Cities and the Terror is slowly rising. But what if… What if you just hide it? 

”But where” you may ask. And that’s where Caches come in. 

Cache is a new type of building, and its purpose is to let you hide things from the government’s eyes. You can build two types of Caches - Dugouts and Subterreant Storages with different storage sizes which will be useful in different stages of the game or for different purposes. These buildings are hidden and they won’t get attention if you’re not in the process of hiding or taking out the money. 

Feel like a real Capo with hidden caches all around the country! You can hide the excesses for a rainy day when you need to pay a bribe or need some extra cash for laundering buildings. You can, of course, build multiple stashes, and don’t be afraid that some police car will notice them! 

Of course, there’s also a catch - Cartel Tycoon can be a harsh game after all! When your money is hidden in stashes, it will deteriorate over time. There are all kinds of critters underground, so if you forget about your stash for a couple of years you might find an empty storage and a very fat rat. 

We can’t wait for you to check out these buildings and hide dirty money all over your property!

[h3][b]III. PLAYTEST ːcartel_loveː[/b][/h3]

[h3]The playtest of the upcoming update will be starting this week![/h3] We’ll post all of the links on Steam and our Discord! 

We’re still playing around with the sizes of Caches and with new combat mechanics, so during the playtest, we’ll need your help to figure all of this out and release the update with your feedback in mind!

[previewyoutube=A4vTSsjvveY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Hola Capos! It’s Andrey! It’s been a month since the Goals & Gains Update, and we’re here to bring you another one! “The Sacred Lamb” Update brings you more end-game content, multiple quality-of-life changes, and many-many bug fixes. Let’s get right into it!

Huh, just joking! Don’t forget to like, subscribe and leave comments down below! My Lieutenants are watching you do it. All done? Good, let’s get one with the devlog! 

We’ll start with Special Buildings. “Why?” you may ask. They’re an essential part of the new end-game content coming with the update. In order to access it you’ll need to capture all of the Special Buildings, and a new questline will open to you. If you decide to pursue it, you’ll meet new characters, make tough decisions and acquire desirable unlocks. This questline will test you but believe me, it will be worth it. 

As always, your choices will matter and will lead to different endings, but you’ll be satisfied either way! 

We’ve also updated our Lieutenant List. It’s no longer a Lieutenant list, but a Character List - navigate to your favorite Mayors, Gang Leader-buddies, and, of course, Lieutenants with one menu! No more running your mouse through all of your cities looking for that one Mayor that didn’t give you a loan yet - just find them through the menu!

With this update, we’re also bringing a new type of Lieutenant Ability - the one you can toggle on or off, which gives you more wiggle room and creative ways to use your lieutenants. We want you to feel more in control of your Cartel, and we’ll continue to fight… I mean work in this direction.

And speaking of control, we’re bringing more Advanced Settings to the Sandbox Mode. You’ll be able to control the Events and the Market. You’ll be able to turn them off completely if you so desire, and you’ll be able to control the frequency of the Events and the Market “Difficulty”. Make the Sandbox truly special for yourself! 

We’re also adding the search bar to the Research Tree! Find the desired building or an upgrade in seconds! You loved the Research Queue addition in the last update, so we’re making the Research Tree even more accessible with this update. 

We’re also giving some love to those of you who bought the game called “Cartel Tycoon” but still want a family-friendly endeavor. Your legal packages with nothing illegal inside will no longer draw suspicion from the government which will make building a legal empire an easier task for you! 

And, of course, there will be lots of smaller quality-of-life changes and bug fixes, some of which we spotted ourselves, and some of which you reported on our forums! Thank you for that! 

The Sacred Lamb Update is coming very soon, and we can’t wait for you to check it out! 

Thanks for watching! Subscribe to our socials, and join Discord to chat with the devs and fans and enjoy some exclusive content. See you, Capos!

[expand type=details]Hola Capos! It’s me - Andrey! I haven’t seen you since the 1.0 Release, so it’s good to be back with another devlog! And it’s a big one. Our next update - Goals & Gains is coming very soon, so it’s time for you to know what’s inside. Let’s get right into it! 


[b]Global Goals.[/b] We’ve been hinting about this addition on our socials, and some of you might’ve already figured it out! We’re adding Global Goals to Sandbox Mode - you can choose or simply play without them, but completing a Global Goal will grant you unique goodies - special character skins, for example! 
Global Goals differ and you can decide on how to approach them! And if you fail them - don’t worry, you can keep playing your Sandbox game and try again later!


[b]The Logistics.[/b] When the game hit 1.0, we got a lot of new players and feedback about the logistics part of the game. So we’ve been working on improving it since the release. There are a lot of changes under the hood but with the new system in place, there no longer should be a situation when one of your Workshops is loaded with products and the other ones sit empty. We’ve also adjusted how Residencies distribute Dirty Money between production and city buildings! 

[b]New Events.[/b] With this update, we’re also adding new events that can happen in your game! For example, Building Events that can affect your production, adding more variety to the process. Also, we’re adding Enemy Gang Events - some of which will require a hard choice to make but will spice up your interactions with Gang Leaders and introduce players to some Gang Mechanics they weren’t using before. Did you already know that you can talk to the Gang Leader to better your relationship? With new Gang Events, you certainly will! 

[b]Saving and Loading times.[/b] With the 1.0 Release, a lot of you pointed out that the game sometimes takes too long to save. Since the release, we’ve been optimizing and rewriting the system, so now your games should load and save much faster, and the size of your saves got reduced significantly! We’ll continue monitoring your feedback on this so we can further improve the system but our internal tests look promising! 

[b]Research Tree.[/b] Research Tree also got lots of love in this update - now the game will remember where you were on the Research Tree when you closed it, so you don’t have to find Warehouse III when you open it again. And that’s not all! You can now….. DRUMROLL PLEASE…. Queue research! Yep, you heard me right! Add everything you want to Research to the Queue, pay upfront - and if you changed your mind about Warehouse - just delete it from the queue and get the money back! 

We’ve also made a lot of small visual changes, fixed a lot of bugs, and generally had an awesome time reading all of your feedback and finding ways to implement it into the game. We want to thank everyone who supported our game from the start and those of you who joined us with the 1.0. We’re grateful that you gave Cartel Tycoon a shot, and we want to make the game even better for all of you! 

I know, I know, cut down on the sentimentalities, you’re here to learn about the update and when it’s coming. So here it is...

The Goals & Gains is coming out... TODAY! Go to the stores and update the game! 

Thanks for watching, don’t forget to like and subscribe and also leave your comments down below. Subscribe to our socials, and join Discord to chat with the devs, and fans of the game and enjoy some exclusive content. See you, Capos!

They are - [b]C.A.M.P.O.S, Vicious Seeds, Candeleros, Orkesta Mendoza, Tribilin Sound, Dengue Dengue Dengue & Prisma, and Chico Unicornio![/b] And introducing [b]DJ FARRAPO[/b], who’s working on his tracks for the 1.0 Release right now! With some of them, we’ve been working long before Cartel Tycoon got released - we’ve had our vision for the vibe of the future soundtrack, and these incredible artists perfected it! 

[h2]We talked to some of them about their music, our game, and their passion for it! But first, some introductions.[/h2]

[h3]Let’s talk about [b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] first… officially the group is called Cumbias And More Psychedelic Original Sounds and it started as a side project for Joshua Camp, who’s also has a group called Chicha Libre. He’s been in the industry for well over 20 years now both as a performer, playing a fair amount on Broadway and in touring music groups, and as a songwriter/composer for advertising, TV, films, and now, with Cartel Tycoon, video games![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/ebdc14ff32512b759a2a4fb1dc242a8b5a30706c.png[/img]

 


[h3][b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] has started his musical activity as a keyboard player more than 30 years ago. But soon his career as a DJ took over and that of music producer was added in 2005. At the moment he’s also the band leader of two different projects! [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/c61857120d6d5f6fc0c4f119ff23d894bf186c0d.png[/img]


[h3][b]Triblin Sound[/b] aka Alvaro Ernesto is a Peruvian DJ/producer of electronic and fusion music. He started Tribilin Sound 20 years ago djing with cumbia, salsa, regueros stuff. Then he started producing house/tech music for foreign labels and playing dj sets at radio Miraflores.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/42f0d09b6313366f8a44fa459ab3649d516a430b.png[/img]


[h3]THE INTERVIEW[/h3]

[i]Were there any movies or TV series that inspired you while writing for “Cartel Tycoon”? [/i]

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - The composers Ennio Morricone and Nino Rota are massive influences on me when it comes to instrumental/score writing. They were key elements to Sergio Leone’s westerns and Federico Fellini’s early period of film making, respectively, so I’d have to put them at the top of my list.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - Surely Narcos!
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - TV series like Hawai 5 0, with that special guitar sound from The Ventures. I also get some inspiration in the surf rock sound taken from The Munsters, a tv show from the 60’s and finally the Pulp Fiction theme “Misirlou”, honestly one of the most exciting film intros for sure.


[i]Was it your first foray into the Latin America sound or was is always your passion? [/i]

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] -  I’ve been listening to music from Latin and Central America since I was a young man, but it wasn’t until I co-founded the band Chicha Libre around 2007-2008 that I really started to dig into specific styles of performing & writing, like Chicha and cumbia.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - South American music has always been a great passion of mine and a source of inspiration and research. Till now I've released a Brazilian album and several remixes and singles of Latin American music, like my last one "El Cabron '', an instrumental electrocumbia in which the lead themes are played by a Colombian gaita.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - It is always my passion. I really dig latam folklore. I like to travel in order to discover new instruments, and be in touch of new forms of making music. And collab with artist around America.


[i]Have you ever been to Latin America yourself or do you just have the feeling for it? [/i]

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - Yes I’ve toured and also visited several times to Colombia, Mexico, Peru, Brazil, Chile, and Puerto Rico. I definitely have tried to make the most of those experiences in terms of learning and listening as much I can.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - I've traveled and toured in Brazil several times. 
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - Sure, Im from Peru so here you can find diversity in all kinds: art, music, food. All those experiences are great in order to make music with a “Latin American” feeling into it.


[i]If your music had words, who is your dream LatAm singer? [/i]

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - Oh I would definitely go old-school and have ‘El Cantante’ Hector Lavoe on a track!
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - Difficult question... anyway in this period I would like to do a collaboration with Eva De Marce. Do you know that Wagner Moura, the actor who plays Pablo Escobar in Narcos is also an excellent singer? I played with him about 10 years ago in São Paulo (BR)!
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - My favorite singer is Hector Lavoe. Music like “Loco”, “Todo tiene su final” and “El cantante” is all I need for a great party. I also love all the Ruben Blades lyrics. And don’t forget Tengo Calderon.


What should players feel when they hear your music in-game? 

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - Hopefully they will feel fully immersed in the experience and the music will help get them ‘in the zone’ so to speak.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - Excitement!
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - They must feel the latino thing, those latin vibes, percussions, that misterious mood that brings my tracks. Players must feel tension and fear of what will happen later in the game


A lot of people asked us if there going to be more music on full release… Are you working on something?

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - Yes indeed! I’m currently working on a new killer track. It’s got groove and attitude in spades.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] -  Of course, I'm always working on new music. I have several projects and upcoming releases of different styles: some electro swing and some urban/latin stuff.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - Sure, I think it is just the beginning in the search of new sounds. Im really excited making some cumbia with that surf rock guitar sound and dub things. I hope Cartel Tycoon gives me the opportunity to send more of my more recently music I’ve made.


Tell us a bit about your creative process. What does it start with? 

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - With this style of music, I always start with finding the perfect groove and feel in terms of the rhythm section and looping. Then I start improvising around those grooves to get the main melodic ideas and then 90 percent of the process in terms of hours spent, is just refining those initial improv ideas until it’s a tight arrangement.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - There is no single way, sometimes I start from a melodic idea, other times from a harmonic progression, or even a sample or a bass line.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - It starts with the feeling or emotion I want to be part of all the music. I usually like to make interpolations from other tracks. I like to live on the edge with the music deadline (lol)


Have you worked on any other games soundtracks or maybe other media (TV, Films, etc.)?

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - This is my first video game I’ve worked on, which is very exciting, but I have had many years writing for film, television and advertising: Tv shows like Weeds, Homeland, On My Block, Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt. Advertisements for Mac Cosmetics, Sephora, Ralph Lauren, and tons more like that.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - A long time ago I started a collaboration project with a video game company from my hometown Bologna, but in the end nothing came of it. However I did the soundtrack for several short films, exhibitions, commercials and one of my songs is also included in the soundtrack of the famous TV series Shameless.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - Sure, I’ve made some stuff for some brands here in Peru (Hapag-Lloyd German tracking company, ISM Group (Loa Water). Actually im learning the process of making a soundtracks for a movie.


Do you play video games? What are the latest games you played?

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] -  I run hot and cold with video games but I’ve played them all my life. My last obsession was Alto’s Odyssey: The Lost City. The music and sound design are great.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - I used to play Asphalt, but now I'm totally absorbed by my job.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - Sure, I like to play Counter Strike. The first videogame I really enjoyed was Half-Life I.


What’s your favorite soundtrack from any other game, film, TV?

[b]C.A.M.P.O.S[/b] - Like a lot of people in the industry this past year we’ve all been digging Hans Zimmer’s score to Dune, ridiculously good! The tv show Severance, which I’m currently watching, has a fantastic score by Theodore Shapiro.
[b]DJ FARRAPO[/b] - There's so many. A very good Latin America soundtrack is that of the movie City Of God. In general I am very passionate about Morricone's soundtracks, which are a source of continuous inspiration for me.
[b]Triblin Sound[/b] - I love all Ennio Morricone music: the Untouchables, Cinema Paradiso. The music selection from Tarantino’s movies. The Unsolved Mysteries Theme, the San Junipero soundtrack from Black Mirror Netflix series.

 

[h3]Of course, music continues to live and evolve after it gets to us - every song finds its place in the game, and our whole team works with the artists to create the perfect soundtrack to Cartel Tycoon together. If you want to feel the vibes of the game outside of playing you can now get the full soundtrack on all the major platforms! As promised, we’re leaving the links below:[/h3]

notes.title: Balance Update is LIVE
notes.notes:
[h2]Hola, Capos! [/h2]

[h3]Our Balance Update is now live across all the platforms! The Update is out of the Beta, and in it, we have implemented a less punishing Terror system, reworked Attention Stars, gave your Lieutenants another useful function, and introduced many balance changes to the game that ultimately give you more choice in your playstyle! 

We'll continue working on further Balance changes and system reworks, and will have more for you in our next Major Update - Special Buildings!

As always, thank you for your support and we'll see you on the lands of Cartel Tycoon! [/h3]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/dadf7ac8e9c5c331a16706099415acacb58a313e.png[/img]

[h3]Cartel Tycoon v 0.9.3.2610 (January Balance Update)[/h3]

[h2]Major changes[/h2]

ːcartel_loveː [b]Major Terror rework:[/b] We wanted to make Terror less punishing, and that’s why now Terror reduces over time by itself and Attention Stars deactivate after the attack. The Terror scale has been changed, and now gaining each new Attention Star will require more Terror. We’ve also added more ways to gain Terror to balance things out. We will continue working on the Terror system in future updates.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Major attacks rework:[/b] We’re also introducing changes to Attention Star attacks themselves: Order of Attention Stars has been changed. Now it’s: Police, Federales, DEA, National Army, CIA, US Army. New Attack type added for Police - Road Cordons which will block roads for a limited amount of time (don’t send your Lieutenants there), Federales now arrest buildings, DEA now searches multiple buildings, the “Investigation” attack has been removed. US Army follows your Lieutenants even if you move them.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Major Village rework:[/b] With this update, we wanted to make interactions with Villages more complex and fun: Villages are now upgradable, upgrades unlock new legal products. You are now able to choose the price for legal products in Villages. Buying for a higher price grants you more Loyalty, taking products for free rises your Terror. You can now use Dirty Money to buy products from villages.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Smuggling points rework:[/b] We wanted to make Smuggling Points more money-efficient and also introduce new ways to use your Lieutenants. The delivery time now also includes product loading time. Smuggling Points now have 1 Delivery Slot, each Lieutenant stationed in the Smuggling Point will grant an additional Delivery Slot. Each Smuggling point has a different amount of additional Delivery Slots. You can now sell illegal products without packaging in all Smuggling Points, but selling them this way through Seaports and Border Checkpoints will grant you, additional Terror. You can sell packed drugs in all the Smuggling Points also.

ːcartel_loveː Global Unlocks rework: All of the regions have been removed from Global Unlocks, you can use all of them in Sandbox and Survival Modes without additional unlocks now! Conditions for unlocking Pathos Residence were changed. Players who already unlocked it will keep it. We will continue to improve the Global Unlocks system in future updates. 

Quest-Events rework: We feel like Quest-Events brought more storytelling variety to the game, but also ːcartel_loveː brought more challenge, especially in the early game - we wanted to address it in this update. More Quest-Events were added, and now you’ll see more positive Quest-Events that will help you grow your Empire. Lieutenants Quest-Events appear more often now.

ːcartel_loveː [b]Lieutenants' experience no longer grows when they’re idle. [/b]Now If you want your Lieutenants to gain XP, you’ll have to use them!  

[h2]Balance[/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Market Balance has been changed:[/b] Base prices for Opium and Dried Cannabis have been lowered, their price on the Market will change more frequently but in a smaller range. Base prices for Meth and Cocaine have been increased, their price on the Market will change less frequently but in a larger range, The market also won’t affect Opium and Cannabis at the start of the game that much.
[*] Survival Mode balance has changed to reflect the current Balance changes.
[*] The Cannabis production Balance has been tweaked.
[*] Efficiency Layers have been changed across difficulty levels of Sandbox Mode.
[*] Difficulty levels for Sandbox have been changed: Easy now has 5 neutral regions, Normal has 3 neutral regions.
[*] The speed of cars on sand and gravel roads has been lowered, and the speed of cars on all the roads has been reworked.
[*] Prices of roads have been lowered.
[*] Prices and Upkeep Costs of these Tier I buildings in the Research Tree have been lowered: Farm, Warehouse, Transport Company, Workshop, River Pier.
[*] Prices of Passive Effects on Tier I of Research Tree have been lowered in half.
[*] Cities now lose control over the course of 16 days.
[*] Workshop Upgrades has been changed: drugs won’t need additional research, only the packaging
[*] One delivery of Dirty Money to Laundering Buildings now lasts for a larger amount of Laundering cycles. Storage capacities of Laundering Buildings now reflect this change, and now they can be overflowed.
[*] Your Starting Region now may have an enemy and arrested buildings on the start. The Player still controls the Smuggling Point of the Region.
[*] Confiscation now lasts 12 days instead of 7.
[*] You can construct a Stadium and a Catherdral in any city now. (But still 1 on the Map)
[*] The time between Mayor Favors has been increased.
[*] Mayor Favor “Lower Terror” now lowers much more Terror, and you can’t get Attention Stars while it happens.
[*] Price for Mayor Favor: Arrest Removal has been increased.
[*] You gain more Loyalty for City Events
[*] Construction of non-city buildings now grants a bit of Loyalty.
[*] Building Demolition with Lieutenant Ability now grants you 90% of the building cost instead of 50%.
[*] The highest Lieutenants' upkeep price during the negotiation phase is now higher.
[*] Conditions of some Deals with Lieutenants have been updated - more products need to be sold.
[/list]

 

[h2]Other updates & changes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Lieutenants now require a certain level of Terror to be recruited. 
[*] An Assassination of your Lieutenant that you ordered will lower the Allegiance of all other Lieutenants in the Cartel.
[*] Silent Assassination ability won’t rise Terror anymore. But it lowers the Allegiance of all Lieutenants.
[*] A lot of minor adjustments and updates to Lieutenant Abilities to bring them up to the current balance changes.
[*] Multiple Tutorial changes to reflect the new update and improve the experience.
[*] 
[/list]
 

[h2]Visual[/h2]

[*] City Menu now shows all of the Mayor Favors. No need to start a dialogue every time you need a favor! 
[*] New Animation added to Terror Scale to signal the moment it starts lowering.

[*] Hotel and Residence can no longer send money to neutral buildings.
[*] Fixed: Dirty Money for construction doesn’t deliver to Charity Houses

notes.title: Surprise BETA Update // Devlog 18
notes.notes:
[h2]Surprise Beta Balance Update right before the Holidays is here! Check out our newest devlog! [/h2]

[previewyoutube=T5P0_E6l3Ug;full][/previewyoutube]


[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 
The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

Ho-ho-hola everyone! Hi! My name is Andrey, and I’m the community manager for Cartel Tycoon. The year is almost over, and we want to bring you yet another update! This time we’ve focused on balancing the game around your feedback, and will also introduce some experimental features! Let’s get right into it. 
 
As we have said in our latest Q&A video (by the way, watch it if you haven’t already) we’re looking at ways to expand, balance, and rework our Terror mechanics. The changes to Terror mechanic is something our players were asking for a while now, and we were looking for a way to introduce the changes while not breaking other systems in place. This update introduces our first steps in this direction! Right now, it’s only beneficial for players to keep Terror at the lowest level possible, and rising Terror brings nothing but trouble. We want to introduce more Terror mechanics that actually encourage players to rise it to higher levels. Let’s talk about balancing and reworking Terror first.
 
First of all, Attention Stars aren’t permanent anymore! We know that will make a lot of people happy! We have reworked the mechanic of all the agencies' attacks, and now they will be happening in waves, like in that mission in the “That Sinking Feeling” campaign. You know the one. Attention Star will light up when the attack wave is about the happen, and after it ends, the Star will deactivate. That means that the attacks themselves will become more persistent - for example, the CIA will follow your lieutenants if you try to move them and will blow up all the buildings that the lieutenant has been in. We’ve also added a new type of attack - Police roadblocks! They will block you out of certain areas and will put more pressure on your production - don’t let your trucks with valuable products move through them! The roadblocks won’t be there forever, of course, you’ll need to wait a couple of days or just… bribe the cops, and they’ll be out of your hair.
 
“But Andrey, the Terror still stays on the same level, and these kinds of changes will only make it harder!” Well, not anymore! Now the Terror will lower by itself! It won’t be fast but if you act like a law-abiding citizen for some time, the Terror level will reflect that! The more Stars you have the slower it lowers, so if you just got to the first Star, you won’t have to worry too much. We’ve also moved Stars a bit on the Terror scale, and for each new Star, you’ll have to gain more Terror than before. Of course, we DID add more ways for you to gain Terror.
 
And now about expanding the Terror mechanic. You’ll be able to sell illegal goods for Terror in Seaports and Checkpoints without the need to package the goods! Less work for you, but more Terror! Some of the lieutenants that are available to hire will also tie with your Terror level. So if you want to hire a certain one for your Cartel, you’ll need to show him your power of intimidation! And your Terror level will also play a crucial role in keeping your lieutenants happy! Some of them enjoy being a part of the peaceful cartel, so if you start any wars, these lieutenants won’t be happy! Of course, some of them joined for the blood and smell of gun powder, so they will enjoy your more… destructive activities. And, there’s more Terror to gain when purchasing legal products from Villages. Let’s talk about that a bit.
 
Villages are getting a massive rework in this update. First of all, we’re introducing Tiers of villages - you’ll be able to upgrade them, and in return, upgraded villages will sell you more types of legal products. We’re also changing the way you’re purchasing from villages: now you can use your Dirty Money to purchase the products, and you’ll be able to set your own prices and face the consequences. If you’re a generous Capo and offer more money for the products, you’ll gain more loyalty. If, however, you want to be feared, and just take whatever you want, be prepared for your Terror level to rise.
 
But this update is called Balance Update, not Terror Update, so let’s talk about general balance changes we’re introducing to the game. We’ve changed our Market mechanic so it won’t affect your early game too much. Prices for Opium and Cannabis won’t be that affected by the Market, but the mid and late-game drugs will require you to experiment, research, and generally keep an eye on the market. 
Another balance change is coming to Quest-Events. Now, “positive” events that are actually helping the player to expand and grow will be happening much more frequently, and we hope that you’ll love this change. 
Also, smuggling points now sell twice as much product! And we’ve also added loading and unloading times to smuggling points so they won’t start sending cargo as soon as you turn them on - you’ll have time to deliver your product and sell it in a bunch, without paying for empty boats and planes! 
We’ve also balanced growing zones around the map, so we’re excited for you to try the regions you haven’t considered before!  There are more mechanics in the works that are scheduled for our next big update, so we’re excited for you to try out this experimental build and leave your feedback on our Discord server!
Oh, and I almost forgot! We have removed locked regions from the Global Unlocks menu so you can enjoy any region you want in a Sandbox game, without the need to conquer them in the Story Mode!
 
There are also, of course, smaller balance changes that will be reflected in the Patch Notes, and bug fixes. And a lot more stuff is in the works for the Special Building update that will be coming after this one. Unique Mayor Quests, anyone? We’ve got a lot more in store, and want to thank everyone who supported the game through the year! But enough about the future, let’s get back to today. You can playtest the Balance Update right now if you join our Discord! We can’t wait to hear your feedback, so what are you waiting for!
 
Are you excited to play the new update of Cartel Tycoon? Write your impressions in the comments, and don’t forget to subscribe here, on YouTube, and on our socials! Share your thoughts about the game we’re building together!

Hey! My name is Andrey, and I’m the community manager for Cartel Tycoon. Today I want to tell you about exciting new features coming in the October Update this week![b] Yes, you heard me right - this week, on October 7th! [/b]From Russia With Love update was the biggest we’ve had so far, so we got a lot of feedback from you, so that’s what we’re focusing on primarily in this update. Let’s jump right into it.

First of all, [b]we’re completely reworking the research line, making it an actual upgrade tree[/b], and implementing lots of your suggestions as branches on that tree! The main idea behind this change is to make research less of a linear process and more of a proactive gameplay mechanic that provides you with meaningful choices that will benefit the growth of your empire. [b]You will be able to independently upgrade storage, productivity, and the number of cars the building has![/b] For example, you can focus on making your Aerodromes sell more products at a faster rate! Or add more trucks to your Transport Company! Of course, it will cost you, but it will be worth the price. Upgrades to your existing buildings will open new research paths for you, which will help you shape your empire the way you like it. 


[b]Another big part of the update is the new Quest-Events[/b]. Your lieutenants can bring you important and urgent news at any time, and it’s up to you to decide the outcome. These events have been in the works for a while now. We’re so happy to present you with the first version of our vision. We want our players to experience more narrative challenges and make the world of Cartel Tycoon more lively. [b]These events will offer you more ways to deal with Terror, Loyalty, and Allegiance![/b] Your lieutenants tell you that DEA is snooping around your smuggling points? Listen to them, build or capture a new one, and the Allegiance of all your lieutenants will rise. Dismiss them, and their Allegiance will drop. Are villagers scared of your expanding empire? Buy something from them to show them how generous you can be - all while bringing your Terror down. The choice is always yours.


Another upcoming feature is something you’ve been asking for for a while, [b]new lieutenant abilities![/b] We’re bringing you two new ones. The first one makes your research go faster. With the expansion of our Research Tree, we felt that it was necessary to give you a way to speed it up. 
And the other one, well, rises your Terror. Yes, you heard it right. We want to test out negative abilities with this update. We feel like this change will impact the recruitment process and give way to some exciting scenarios. What do you think about it? Let us know in the comments!


Of course, more goodies are coming with this update. [b]We’ve optimized the games’ performance[/b], added a fancy new loading screen, [b]heard your feedback on the new market feature[/b], and made some changes there - along with a tooltip. Also, we finetuned this feature across the game modes: previous settings distracted players from their main objectives too much! We’ve also made more tips for the Tutorial and made the “Needs and Fears” campaign more beginner-friendly! And now you can choose which Story Mode campaign you want to play! Along with that, [b]we made some adjustments to Deals with lieutenants[/b] - now they’ll give you a fixed price for the product, which won’t be affected by the Market. Of course, [b]bug fixes, minor adjustments will also be in the patch notes.[/b]


Once again, the October Update is coming this week, but starting today, [b]you can join a closed beta test of the upcoming features![/b] Just join our official Discord server for more information. Do it, do it now!

notes.title: From Russia With Love Update Announcement
notes.notes:
[h2]Hola Capos! ːcartel_loveː

Today we want to announce our next update - From Russia With Love. It will be hitting the stores on August 23! [/h2]

In this update, we’ve decided to focus on the core gameplay mechanics of Cartel Tycoon. We want our game to be “easy to learn, hard to master,” and not just “hard.” That’s why we’re introducing multiple reworks to our logistics, a full tutorial, and so much more. Of course, there’s also an entirely new campaign for Story Mode - with new characters, hard decisions, multiple endings, and Global Unlocks. Welcome to… 

[h2]From Russia With Love Update[/h2]

[previewyoutube=AxLoJ9nucK8;full][/previewyoutube]

[list]
[*] [b]Complete Story Released!![/b] New characters, storylines, and rewards!
[*] [b]Revamped Logistics[/b]. Flexible filters for cargo, Warehouse and Workshop overhaul, and brand new Transportation Company building
[*] [b]Dynamic Supply and Demand.[/b] The prices are now affected by your actions
[*] [b]River Pier. [/b] A new way to smuggle the goods!
[*] [b]Castle Residence and Collector's Residence.[/b] Unlock them by beating the challenges!
[*] [b]Full Tutorial.[/b] Basics of Cartel Tycoon explained step-by-step.

[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/02dc8d4543889cd4e10a6452bee09b5a60aca50d.png[/img]

ːcartel_menaceː With this update, we’re adding our next chapter to Story Mode of Cartel Tycoon. It’s an entirely [b]new campaign called “That Sinking Feeling.”[/b] Your Capo will meet a Columbian playboy, a Russian gangster, and a “businesswoman” from Miami. You all want the same thing - to achieve your wildest dreams. Can you trust them enough to do it together? That’s for you to decide. Your relationships with these characters will directly impact how this story plays out and what will be waiting for you at the end of the journey. A friend by your side and a region at your feet? A personal helicopter and your own submarine? Or a bullet in the back and an empire in flames.  

ːcartel_menaceː We’ve gathered your feedback and [b]reworked our logistics gameplay loop[/b] to make it much more enjoyable and easier to understand and control. A new building is added to the mix, and we’ve reworked some old ones. More details in this devlog episode (link)

ːcartel_menaceː We’ve added [b]dynamic prices to illegal products[/b], and your actions directly affect them. It means that you’ll have to adapt and modify your empire to bring more profit. We think that this feature makes the gameplay more fun and interactive for the players, even those of you who thought they’ve already figured out the best way to become rich in Cartel Tycoon.

ːcartel_menaceː [b]River Pier is a new type of smuggling point [/b]coming to the game. It’s already on the map, you just need to capture and upgrade it to start using it. Upper tiers of this new building are Global Unlocks from the upcoming campaign in Story Mode!

ːcartel_menaceː [b]Two new types of Residences[/b] are coming to the game. [b]Castle Residence[/b] makes the life of your Capo easier by giving him a helicopter, and [b]Collectors Residence[/b] makes the life of your lieutenants easier - by giving them faster cars. 

ːcartel_menaceː The overwhelming demand for a more[b] detailed step-by-step tutorial[/b] made us realize we have to shift our plans and deliver it right now. We’ll be waiting for your feedback to make it even better.  


Those who closely follow the development process may find that [b]many features mentioned above weren’t on our Roadmap for the August Update[/b]. The reason for that being that we wanted to focus our attention on the core gameplay of Cartel Tycoon and make it as enjoyable and fluid as possible - for new players and veteran Capos alike.

This shift means that [b]we have to postpone the release of the fully-functioning Special Buildings[/b]. We understand that this might frustrate you, but we decided that it is more important to make the core mechanics and approachability of the game better before adding something that doesn’t directly impact the gameplay. We’re working on the buildings, don’t worry, and we’re making them even more “special,” they will be a part of the future updates - just not this one. 

That’s it for today. We hope you enjoyed this peek at the From Russia With Love Update - more changes are coming, and we’ll mention all of them in the upcoming Patch Notes, but today we just wanted to talk about the major things. 

Let us know in the comments if you have more questions! 

Keep an eye on our social channels for all the latest news and updates, and be sure to [url=https://discord.gg/Cf674c8b]join the official Cartel Tycoon Discord[/url] to join the community, share your feedback, and chat with the development team.

notes.title: Cartel Tycoon Prosperity Update Announcement & Roadmap Update
notes.notes:
[h2]Hola, Capos!

Happy to announce that Prosperity Update with major new content and features will arrive in two weeks, on June 23.[/h2]

Today, we want to tell you more about both our short-term and long-term plans: what we have prepared in store for June 23 and also share more details on how our roadmap has recently evolved (multiplayer and enemy AI are getting more love now!).

Also, you can buy Cartel Tycoon on Steam with a 20% discount right now to prepare for the new update! Tell your friends!

[h2]Prosperity Update[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/11ce0223bbc7d290e0ce09e331ff239aa7a8fd20.png[/img]


[olist]
[*] Our new buildings bring new exciting ways to fit the style of your Capo and your own playstyle: introducing [b]Paranoid, Party, Pretentious and Modern Residences[/b]. We did not want the difference to be purely cosmetic, so we ended up giving each type of Residence its own unique mechanics. More details [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1220140/eventcomments/5296777170369513872?snr=2_groups_partnerevents_]in this post[/url] and devlog episode:
[previewyoutube=dW2xserFGgs;full][/previewyoutube]



[*] With the previous update we introduced customized difficulties - this time we are taking it even further and [b]making lots of parameters in Sandbox customizable at the game start[/b]. Want to keep the authorities passive while keeping the challenge of production optimization? Maybe you want to play normally but start with all researches unlocked? Or how about putting everything on the highest difficulty but start with a big load of money to build lots of stuff right away? Now you can do all that, and more, and we cannot wait for you to share to hear your reports on the most fun ways to play Cartel Tycoon with us... and other players! [b]Yes, other players will be able to try out your customized settings![/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/4c9d4a9cfbc5139085ce0b11734af49ae3e72de9.png[/img]


[*] And for those who want a pure hardcore permadeath experience, we have added [b]Survival Mode[/b]! No manual saves, a couple of dollars in your pocket, lots of enemies and imminent death on the horizon. Your Capo took a deal he shouldn’t have taken and now you have to use all of your abilities to survive. Take a long walk before starting a game in a Survival Mode and be sure you’re experienced enough to be ready to face the challenges. Or, maybe you just like that sweet-sweet suffering.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/574a40a4f95084e3e940c2b1fcf25955d932d6eb.png[/img]


[*] Last but not least, we’re introducing [b]Global Progression![/b] In this update we’ve added Special Challenges to the Story Mode! If you complete them - you will be able to unlock new starting bosses and regions for Sandbox & Survival Modes! For now, there are 4 unlockable characters in total: would you be able to catch ‘em all? More updates to Global Progression are on the way!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/a9fdcbbc09982700b1674c43d73064a206645614.png[/img]
[/olist]


[b]The Prosperity update is being released on June 23.[/b] What happens after it is live? As usual, we will closely watch your reports and great feedback and make sure the major bugs are being fixed right away. But let’s talk about our long-term plans - moving forward to the topic of our...

[h2]Development Roadmap[/h2]

First of all, our Development Roadmap now also [url=https://www.carteltycoon.com/roadmap]lives on our own website[/url], as well as [url=https://trello.com/b/I3Ja70gQ/cartel-tycoon-development-roadmap]in Trello[/url]. Some of you have already noticed that we've made some significant updates to it, so please take a look at the updated version (and as usual, please keep in mind that, like anything else in game development, these plans are subject to change)

After the Prosperity update is released, we want to deliver another two major updates around August and October, and then finally release 1.0, targeting somewhere between Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 for it. It is a few months later than we initially had planned, but hear the good news - [b]we are setting ourselves a goal to ship multiplayer as a part of our 1.0 release!
[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/13c5708f6b94f8516782ebce27d0ca85ce55cdd3.png[/img]

Going to be challenging, but absolutely worth it; can’t wait to give you all the way to give good ol’ plata o plomo to your Steam friends. 

Another big addition many of you are going to be happy about: [b]advanced AI for enemy gangs[/b] is now officially part of the plan!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36613041/4c1dd92712cb16c47b0ab9021ddc1d472f5ea956.png[/img]

They are going to become like cartels equal to your own: you will be able to communicate with their leaders, make alliances, and of course burn them to the ground to make a space for yourself. This is also a challenging task, but having good AI opponents just goes so well with the possibility of co-op gameplay we are investing in! Won’t disappoint you.

In conclusion, a few words about our [b]August update[/b]: it doesn’t have a name yet and the scope can change depending on your feedback to Prosperity Update, but we can already tell that it is going to be no less than it! [b]Military Base, Guerrillas and other unique buildings[/b] are going to be part of it, as well as the grand finale of our storyline (you’ll like it), and more!

That’s it for today. Hope you enjoyed this peak to our plans - let us know in the comments if you have more questions. Keep an eye on our social channels for all the latest news and updates, and be sure to [url=https://discord.gg/Cf674c8b]join the official Cartel Tycoon Discord[/url] to join the community, share your feedback, and chat with the development team.

notes.title: Devlog #10 - Steam Early Access Update
notes.notes:
Check out our latest Dev Log below, which covers the updates and features we've released since our Steam Early Access launch in March.

[h3]Devlog #10 - Steam Early Access Update[/h3]
[previewyoutube=gRFhowik8KI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Prefer the written word? We've got you covered. 

The full transcript is available below:[/h3]

On behalf of the team at Moon Moose and tinyBuild, thank you for all of your support and feedback throughout this first stage of Cartel Tycoon’s Early Access! Four weeks have passed since our Early Access release on March 18, and it was a very busy time for us! During those four weeks, we have released 4 big patches and 4 smaller hotfixes. For this episode of our Devlog, we’ll provide an overview of all major new features we’ve added in those patches!

Managing a cartel should be sufficiently challenging - it is an illegal enterprise, after all - but it should definitely not be tedious. With that in mind, we improved building automation and added new quality of life features to help streamline your empire management.

The first of these features is a new animated UI element that visualizes the logistical connections between your buildings. When enabled, this new feature will draw a color-coded line between the selected building and those within its logistical network - including those outside the building’s radius of influence. This can be helpful to understand at a glance how your empire is connected, and make adjustments where necessary. 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/8LIJAbB.gif[/img]

We’ve also added features to help streamline the flow of Dirty Money and reduce the frequency with which a player must manually interact with buildings to manage upkeep. These new features include helpful UI elements to highlight areas where Dirty Money is no longer available, as well as the new “Pause” status for buildings that lack the necessary funds for upkeep. When a building is Paused, it will automatically re-enable itself once Dirty Money has been delivered.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6eGlg1P.gif[/img]

In our most recent update, we made a host of improvements to the Building List - including a highly requested feature that allows players to swap building Upkeep between Dirty and Legal Money. This is especially useful when you need to make changes to a large number of buildings at once, or adjust to a sudden shift in available funds.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/MpPNz7F.gif[/img]

We’ve also made updates to overall game balance - including highly requested improvements to Terror acquisition and Lieutenant experience gain - and we’ve overhauled a number of UI elements along the command bar at the bottom of the screen. 

All improvements we’ve made thus far were inspired by and improved upon by your feedback. There’s plenty more big and small changes to come, and we will now be slowly shifting our focus from immediate quality of life changes to adding new mechanics and brand new content - including Prisons, new border types, new resources, and much, much more.

For more details on upcoming features and plans, please check out our official development roadmap.

Join the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/carteltycoon]Cartel Tycoon Discord[/url] to learn more and chat with the development team - and be sure to follow us on social media for all the latest news and updates.
